question: How do I compare roofing estimates when the prices are very different?
why_care: A major home expense is easier to assess when the scope is clear.
angle: Build a side-by-side scope checklist before comparing the total.

evidence.title: FTC: Avoid home improvement scams
evidence.finding: Compare written estimates and investigate differences in scope, materials and price.

question: What should I check before hiring a contractor who knocked on my door?
why_care: People need room to make a decision without pressure.
angle: A short checklist of credentials, written terms and payment questions.

evidence.title: FTC: Avoid home improvement scams
evidence.finding: Check licensing and insurance, read the agreement, and avoid pressure to pay in full upfront.

question: Does a drafty room mean I need new windows?
why_care: Comfort and household costs matter before a homeowner considers a replacement.
angle: Start with an assessment of where air enters; avoid promising replacement will solve everything.

evidence.title: CSU Extension: Air sealing Colorado homes
evidence.finding: Drafts can come from gaps throughout the home. A professional energy audit can help identify air leaks; windows and doors are only part of the picture.

question: What should I ask about drafts around an exterior door?
why_care: An uncomfortable entryway can become an everyday frustration.
angle: Explain assessment, weather-stripping and replacement as different conversations.

evidence.title: CSU Extension: Air sealing Colorado homes
evidence.finding: Gaps around doors can admit unwanted airflow; air sealing needs to preserve appropriate ventilation.

question: Which roof coverage questions should I take to my insurance agent?
why_care: Uncertainty about coverage makes an already large decision harder.
angle: Prepare questions about the actual policy; do not predict coverage or a claim outcome.

evidence.title: Colorado Division of Insurance: Homeowner and HOA toolkit
evidence.finding: Colorado provides insurance information and FAQs for homeowners and HOAs. Use the toolkit to prepare policy-specific questions for the insurer.

question: What insurance questions should an HOA board collect before planning exterior work?
why_care: Board members need a shared list of questions before a large maintenance decision.
angle: Create a meeting agenda covering current coverage, project scope and questions for the association's professionals.

evidence.title: Colorado Division of Insurance: Homeowner and HOA toolkit
evidence.finding: The state publishes a dedicated insurance toolkit for homeowners and HOAs; individual coverage must be confirmed with the insurer.

question: What belongs in a written siding or painting estimate?
why_care: Clear expectations help homeowners compare the work they are buying.
angle: Ask about preparation, materials, boundaries of the work and written changes.

evidence.title: FTC: Avoid home improvement scams
evidence.finding: Written estimates should describe the work, materials, completion expectations and price.

question: How can a property manager make contractor bids easier to compare?
why_care: A consistent scope gives decision makers a clearer basis for comparing proposals.
angle: Share a reusable checklist for requesting and reviewing written bids.

evidence.title: FTC: Avoid home improvement scams
evidence.finding: Get multiple written estimates and ask about discrepancies before deciding.
